howItWorks.title: What the device is doing
howItWorks.p1: The device boots when a button is pressed or RPM is detected. It then finds the closest track and loads all of that track's courses into memory.
howItWorks.p2: Race mode is selected automatically as soon as RPM is detected.
howItWorks.p3: When your speed reaches a set threshold, a waypoint is dropped and the device starts monitoring every start/finish and sector line at once. When you reach that waypoint again, it compares the distance driven, finds the course with the nearest length match — one where you've also crossed several of its lines — selects that course, and drops the rest. That registers your first lap with an accurate first-lap time, and from there it counts laps as normal.

guide.title: How the simulator works
guide.lead: This is a full simulation of the DovesDataLogger firmware — the exact code the physical device runs, compiled for your browser — for testing, evaluation, and poking around before you build one.

boot.title: Booting
boot.body: The device boots just like the real one. Press any button to skip the GPS lock screen and go straight to the main menu — or simply press Play: about 3 seconds after the GPS locks, the screen moves on by itself.

controls.title: Controls
controls.body: The outer buttons (◀ ▶) move between menu items and race pages; the center button selects. The keyboard works too: ← Enter →.

replay.title: Replaying a session
replay.body: Press Play to replay the recorded session. Race mode engages automatically, the firmware searches for the nearest track, runs course detection, and starts timing laps — the same pipeline the device runs at the track.

ending.title: Ending the session
ending.body: At the end of the replay the kart comes to a stop. Let the session end on its own, or navigate to the END RACE page and press the center button to commit the log file yourself.

review.title: Reviewing
review.body: An ended session is saved to the simulator's temporary storage: open Review in the main menu to load it back and browse its laps, exactly like on the device. (It evaporates when you leave the page.)

guide.pagesTitle: Race mode pages (◀ ▶ to flip through them)

speed.name: Speed
speed.desc: Big current speed with the lap counter

rpm.name: Engine RPM
rpm.desc: Live RPM, with an over-rev warning at the limit

pace.name: Lap Pace
pace.desc: Live +/− delta against your best lap (center button jumps here while moving)

best.name: Best Lap
best.desc: Fastest lap so far, and which lap set it

optimal.name: Optimal Lap
optimal.desc: Theoretical best built from your best sectors

history.name: Lap History
history.desc: Every lap this session; the center button pages through the list

end.name: End Race
end.desc: Center button ends the session and saves the log

guide.note: Note: Bluetooth and USB transfer are not functional in the simulator.
guide.systemTitle: Menu & system pages (the rest of the firmware)

gpsStatus.name: GPS Status
gpsStatus.desc: Every boot lands here: lock state and HDOP up top, one signal bar per satellite below; any button skips it

race.name: Race
race.desc: Jump straight into race mode; logging starts once GPS time locks

reviewList.name: Review: files
reviewList.desc: Browse saved session logs; center button opens one

reviewResults.name: Review: results
reviewResults.desc: Instant replay of a saved session: driver, course, date, best and optimal lap, and the full lap list

transfer.name: Transfer
transfer.desc: Bluetooth (companion-app download) or USB (the SD card as a drive)

camera.name: Camera
camera.desc: Insta360 pairing and status, manual serial entry, and a bench-test menu — the device auto-records your camera when the engine starts

sdFormat.name: SD Format
sdFormat.desc: Boot page for a blank/corrupted SD card: hold Select 3 s to format it on-device

warnings.name: Warnings & faults
warnings.desc: Recoverable notices dismiss with any button; hard faults (no SD card) hold the screen

charging.name: Charging
charging.desc: Plugged-in idle screen; any button wakes the device back to the menu

guide.systemNote: Pages that need real hardware — the USB drive, a paired camera, SD formatting, charging — can't be reached in the simulator.
